# Motion Library

> 225 hand-made web animations and effects. Each one is a single plain JavaScript file with no dependencies: watch it live, read how it works, tune it with sliders, then copy the code or install it with `npx motion-library add <id>`. Every slider is also a CLI flag, so `npx motion-library add confetti --pieces 300` installs it already tuned. Licence: MIT-0.

## Install

- `npx motion-library list` lists every effect.
- `npx motion-library add <id> [--setting value ...]` writes `animations/<id>.js` into the current project (Node 18+).
- Each file's default export takes a sized container element, draws into it and returns a cleanup function.
- `npx motion-library prompt <id>` prints a prompt for an AI coding assistant with the notes, settings and code.
- Source code: https://github.com/AjEckblad/motion-library · npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/motion-library

## Flow & particles

### Curl-noise flow field

Curl-noise flow field is a Canvas effect: divergence-free curl noise; particles never clump. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add curl-flow.

Particles swirl in smooth streams that leave soft trails and never pile up.

Each particle follows the curl of a noise field, which has no sources or sinks; a translucent fill each frame instead of a clear keeps the trails.

Settings: --count 4000 (500 to 8000, step 100; Particles); --speed 1 (0.2 to 3, step 0.1; Speed); --scale 0.0025 (0.0008 to 0.006, step 0.0001; Field scale).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 2.6 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/curl-flow.html

### Drone light show

Drone light show is a WebGL effect: formation changes solved as an assignment problem: sort, then swap. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add drone-show.

A drone fleet lifts off a barge and flies formations over a night city, mirrored in the bay.

Formation slots are matched to drones by banded sorting, then random swaps kept only if they shorten total flight, so no paths cross.

Settings: --drones 1500 (300 to 3000, step 100; Drones); --speed 1 (0.3 to 2, step 0.1; Show speed); --glow 1 (0 to 2, step 0.1; Glow).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 24.9 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/drone-show.html

### Particle life

Particle life is a Canvas effect: asymmetric attraction table between species; lifelike clusters emerge. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add particle-life.

Coloured particles self-organise into cells, worms and hunting swarms that melt and re-form; drag to stir.

Each species pair attracts or repels by an entry in a small asymmetric table, so red can chase green while green flees; neighbours come from a grid.

Settings: --particles 2400 (600 to 4000, step 100; Particles); --species 6 (2 to 8, step 1; Species); --range 0.105 (0.05 to 0.16, step 0.005; Range).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 5.9 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/particle-life.html

### Cloud chamber

Cloud chamber is a Canvas effect: particle tracks drawn as droplet trails that swell, drift and fade. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add cloud-chamber.

Droplet tracks appear in a misty chamber: straight alpha stubs, spiralling electrons and long muon lines.

Each track is a list of droplets that swell, drift and fade; beta electrons scatter and curl in the magnetic field, tightening as they slow.

Settings: --activity 1 (0.2 to 3, step 0.1; Activity); --field 1 (0 to 2.5, step 0.05; Magnetic field); --mist 1 (0 to 2, step 0.05; Mist).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 7.8 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/cloud-chamber.html

### Spiral galaxy

Spiral galaxy is a WebGL effect: stars on log-spiral arms with differential rotation and additive light. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add galaxy.

A spiral galaxy turns slowly, its arms winding as the bright core blooms.

Stars are placed on logarithmic spiral arms and scattered so arms read as density; a flat rotation curve winds them, and additive points make the core glow.

Settings: --stars 40000 (5000 to 80000, step 1000; Stars); --arms 3 (2 to 6, step 1; Arms); --twist 2 (0.5 to 4, step 0.1; Arm twist).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 4.5 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/galaxy.html

### Strange attractor

Strange attractor is a Canvas effect: particles integrating the Aizawa attractor, with fading-canvas trails. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add strange-attractor.

Thousands of glowing particles trace the Aizawa attractor, an apple-like shell with a spine, as the camera turns.

Particles are integrated through the three Aizawa equations each frame and projected in 3D; fading the canvas slightly instead of clearing leaves the trails.

Settings: --particles 2500 (500 to 6000, step 100; Particles); --speed 1 (0.2 to 3, step 0.1; Speed).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 3.3 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/strange-attractor.html

### Slime mould maps Tokyo

Slime mould maps Tokyo is a WebGL effect: sense, turn, step, deposit: agents carve self-reinforcing trail networks. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add physarum.

A slime mould grows a network between the cities around Tokyo, tightening into trunk lines.

Each agent senses trail ahead-left, ahead and ahead-right, turns toward the strongest and deposits more; the trail diffuses and decays, so only used routes survive.

Settings: --agents 384 (128 to 768, step 64; Grid (agents = grid²)); --sensor 0.39 (0.15 to 1, step 0.01; Sensor angle); --decay 0.9 (0.8 to 0.98, step 0.005; Trail decay).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 12.4 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/physarum.html

### Lightning arcs

Lightning arcs is a Canvas effect: midpoint displacement, recursive branches, glow and afterimage. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add lightning.

Branching bolts strike, re-strike rapidly and leave a glowing afterimage.

Midpoint displacement: each segment’s midpoint is pushed sideways at random and the halves split again, with forks; a wide blurred stroke under a thin white core gives the glow.

Settings: --branches 0.5 (0 to 1, step 0.05; Branching); --rate 14 (2 to 30, step 1; Strikes / second).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 4.0 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/lightning.html

### Iron filings

Iron filings is a Canvas effect: segments align to a bar magnet's field and hop onto its flux contours. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add iron-filings.

Steel filings on paper over one hidden bar magnet hop on each tap and settle into the classic loops from pole to pole; drag the magnet.

Each filing aligns with the local field and is pulled toward the nearest contour of the bar's flux function, the sum of each pole's charge times the cosine of its angle from the bar's axis.

Settings: --filings 7000 (2000 to 16000, step 500; Filings); --lines 16 (6 to 40, step 2; Field lines); --taps 0.45 (0.2 to 3, step 0.05; Tap rate).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 9.2 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/iron-filings.html

### Galton board

Galton board is a Canvas effect: per-bead coin tosses stack into a binomial bell curve. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add galton-board.

Beads pour through brass pegs and pile into a bell curve, matching the dashed theory line.

Each row is roughly a coin toss, so landing spots sum to a binomial; beads are real bodies that bounce and stack via a spatial hash.

Settings: --beads 400 (100 to 700, step 20; Beads); --rows 12 (6 to 16, step 1; Rows); --rate 26 (5 to 80, step 1; Beads per second).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 10.7 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/galton-board.html

### Pin art

Pin art is a WebGL effect: instanced pins that only slide forward, so imprints persist. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add pin-art.

A hand, a face and a ripple rise in relief through steel pins; press to push pins back.

Instanced cylinders with domed heads move only forward, so imprints stay until a sweep resets them; a raking light lets taller pins shade lower ones.

Settings: --pins 72 (32 to 110, step 2; Pins across); --depth 1.2 (0.4 to 2, step 0.05; Relief depth); --speed 1 (0.4 to 2, step 0.1; Speed).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 14.4 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/pin-art.html

### 3D paper confetti

3D paper confetti is a Canvas effect: squash by cos(spin) to fake a 3D tumble, two-sided colour. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add confetti.

Paper confetti bursts from two cannons, tumbles and flutters down.

Scaling each piece’s height by the cosine of its spin angle fakes the 3D tumble, and the sign picks front or back colour; heavy drag and flutter bring it down.

Settings: --pieces 160 (40 to 400, step 10; Pieces); --gravity 1 (0.2 to 2, step 0.05; Gravity).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 2.7 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/confetti.html

### Firefly sync

Firefly sync is a Canvas effect: pulse-coupled oscillators: every flash nudges neighbours forward. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add firefly-sync.

Fireflies in a forest drift into flashing as one; the pointer startles the nearby ones.

Mirollo–Strogatz pulse-coupled oscillators: each firefly is a clock that flashes and resets, and every flash it sees nudges its clock forward.

Settings: --fireflies 700 (100 to 1500, step 50; Fireflies); --coupling 0.07 (0 to 0.2, step 0.005; Coupling); --spread 0.05 (0 to 0.2, step 0.005; Clock spread).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 7.9 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/firefly-sync.html

### GPU particles (262k)

GPU particles (262k) is a WebGL effect: positions live in a float texture; a shader moves them all. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add gpu-particles.

A quarter of a million particles stream through 3D curl noise in glowing filaments.

Positions live in a float texture updated by a fragment shader, ping-ponging between two textures; drawing reads each back with texelFetch and blends additively.

Settings: --size 512 (128 to 1024, step 64; Grid (particles = size²)); --speed 1 (0.2 to 3, step 0.1; Speed).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 6.2 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/gpu-particles.html

### Hydrogen orbitals

Hydrogen orbitals is a WebGL effect: metropolis sampling of an exact wavefunction, coloured by phase. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add orbitals.

A cloud of points shows a hydrogen orbital, sloshing as it morphs into the next one.

Metropolis sampling: each point proposes a step and keeps it with probability |ψ(new)|² ÷ |ψ(old)|²; ψ is the exact solution, coloured by its complex phase.

Settings: --grid 512 (128 to 768, step 64; Grid (particles = grid²)); --speed 1 (0.2 to 3, step 0.1; Speed); --glow 1 (0 to 2, step 0.1; Glow).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 14.1 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/orbitals.html

### Roche limit

Roche limit is a WebGL effect: tidal stretching past the Roche limit shears rubble into a ring. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add roche-limit.

A rubble moon spirals into an ice giant, tears into two streams and winds into a ring.

Twenty thousand particles feel the moon’s self-gravity and the planet’s tide, which grows as 1/d³; inner rubble orbits faster, shearing the streams into a ring.

Settings: --particles 20000 (4000 to 40000, step 1000; Particles); --speed 1 (0.3 to 2.5, step 0.1; Speed); --glow 1 (0.2 to 2, step 0.1; Brightness).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 11.5 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/roche-limit.html

### Starling murmuration

Starling murmuration is a Canvas effect: 3D flocking where each bird tracks only seven nearest neighbours. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add murmuration.

A starling flock stretches and folds, and dark waves ripple through it as a falcon dives.

Boids that track a fixed seven nearest neighbours rather than a radius, found with a hash grid; fear passes neighbour to neighbour, which makes the waves.

Settings: --birds 1600 (400 to 3000, step 100; Birds); --falcon 1 (0 to 2, step 0.1; Falcon attacks).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 7.0 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/murmuration.html

### States of matter

States of matter is a Canvas effect: lennard-Jones atoms plus a thermostat: gas, liquid, crystal. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add states-of-matter.

Atoms cool from gas into droplets, a pool and a hexagonal crystal, then melt again.

Lennard-Jones forces between every pair, with a thermostat steering speeds toward a falling target temperature; atoms are coloured by speed and bonds drawn between close neighbours.

Settings: --atoms 950 (300 to 1600, step 50; Atoms); --gravity 1 (0 to 3, step 0.1; Gravity); --cycle 1 (0.4 to 2.5, step 0.1; Cycle speed).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 7.6 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/states-of-matter.html

### Calligraphy brush

Calligraphy brush is a Canvas effect: bristle-by-bristle brush with per-bristle ink and dry-brush streaks. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add calligraphy.

A brush writes 永 stroke by stroke, with dry streaks on long strokes and pooled ink at turns.

The brush is forty bristles in a teardrop footprint that turns with the stroke and spreads with pressure; each carries its own ink and runs dry.

Settings: --pressure 1 (0.5 to 1.6, step 0.05; Pressure); --ink 1 (0.4 to 2, step 0.05; Ink load); --speed 1 (0.4 to 2.5, step 0.1; Speed).

### Harmonograph

Harmonograph is a Canvas effect: summed decaying sines near a simple ratio, slightly detuned. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add harmonograph.

A pen draws a slowly creeping rosette that thins as the swing dies.

The pen position is a sum of four decaying sines with frequencies near a simple ratio like 2:3; the slight detuning makes the loops precess.

Settings: --speed 1 (0.3 to 3, step 0.1; Speed); --decay 0.6 (0.1 to 2, step 0.05; Decay).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 4.0 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/harmonograph.html

### Chladni plate

Chladni plate is a WebGL effect: GPU grains hop by local vibration and settle on nodal lines. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add chladni.

Sand on a vibrating brass plate gathers into figures that shift as the tone rises.

Each grain hops by how hard its spot shakes and slides toward the standing wave’s nodal lines; 65,000 grains live in a float texture on the GPU.

Settings: --grains 256 (128 to 512, step 32; Grid (grains = grid²)); --sweep 1 (0.3 to 3, step 0.1; Sweep speed); --shake 1 (0.3 to 2, step 0.05; Shake).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 10.7 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/chladni.html

### Crystal growth (DLA)

Crystal growth (DLA) is a WebGL effect: diffusion-limited aggregation: manganese oxide grows fern-like dendrites from a crack in limestone. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add dla-crystal.

Black fern-like manganese dendrites creep up a slab of pale limestone from a crack, branching into plumes with a brown halo.

Diffusion-limited aggregation: random walkers stick on first contact, so tips outgrow hollows; dense trunks print thick, and the far tips finer and browner.

Settings: --speed 1 (0.2 to 3, step 0.1; Growth speed); --stickiness 1 (0.1 to 1, step 0.05; Stickiness).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 12.1 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/dla-crystal.html

### Wind tunnel

Wind tunnel is a WebGL effect: GPU lattice Boltzmann solver shedding a Kármán vortex street. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add wind-tunnel.

Smoke lines flow past a cylinder, wing or plate and roll into a vortex street; drag the body.

A D2Q9 lattice Boltzmann solver: nine populations per cell stream and relax toward equilibrium; MacCormack advection keeps the smoke curls sharp.

Settings: --reynolds 220 (60 to 600, step 10; Reynolds number); --speed 1 (0.3 to 2, step 0.1; Speed); --smoke 15 (6 to 30, step 1; Smoke lines).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 16.3 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/wind-tunnel.html

### Fireworks

Fireworks is a Canvas effect: rocket bursts with gravity, drag and five shell types. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add fireworks.

Rockets burst into peonies, willows, crossettes, two-tone shells and glitter; click to launch one there.

Each star has velocity, gravity and drag, with a rule set per shell type; stars keep their last few positions, drawn as tapering additive streaks.

Settings: --rate 1 (0 to 3, step 0.1; Launch rate); --gravity 1 (0.2 to 2, step 0.05; Gravity); --drag 1 (0 to 2, step 0.05; Air drag).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 7.5 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/fireworks.html

### Bokeh

Bokeh is a Canvas effect: circle of confusion: discs grow with distance from the focal plane. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add bokeh.

Out-of-focus lights drift in layers while the focus pulls through, sharpening some and blooming others.

Each light becomes an aperture-shaped disc sized by its distance from the focal plane, with brightness spread over its area; one rimmed sprite, blended additively.

Settings: --blades 6 (0 to 9, step 1; Aperture blades (0 = round)); --count 75 (10 to 250, step 5; Lights); --focus 1 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Focus pull).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 4.8 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/bokeh.html

### Nebula

Nebula is a WebGL effect: domain-warped fbm gas, lit toward a star, with dust lanes. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add nebula.

Magenta and teal gas drifts around a bright star, cut by dark dust lanes, over twinkling stars.

Domain-warped fractal noise folds the gas into filaments; subtracting a density sample taken toward the star lights its facing sides.

Settings: --drift 1 (0 to 4, step 0.05; Drift); --density 1 (0.3 to 2, step 0.05; Gas density); --stars 1 (0 to 2, step 0.05; Stars).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 6.0 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/nebula.html


## Fluid

### Ink fluid

Ink fluid is a WebGL effect: stable fluids: advect, curl, project, repeat. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add ink-fluid.

Ink swirls and spreads as you push through it, and splats on its own.

A GPU Navier–Stokes solver: velocity advects the dye, vorticity confinement keeps swirls alive, and a pressure solve keeps the flow incompressible.

Settings: --curl 30 (0 to 60, step 1; Curl); --dissipation 0.97 (0.9 to 1, step 0.002; Dye persistence); --splatRadius 0.25 (0.05 to 0.8, step 0.01; Splat radius).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 9.5 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/ink-fluid.html

### Liquid image distortion

Liquid image distortion is a WebGL effect: offset texture lookups by flowing noise. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add liquid-distort.

An image ripples like water, rippling harder where the pointer drags through it.

Each pixel samples the texture at a spot shifted by animated noise, and the shift grows near the pointer.

Settings: --strength 0.04 (0 to 0.12, step 0.002; Strength); --speed 0.4 (0 to 1.5, step 0.05; Flow speed).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 4.8 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/liquid-distort.html

### Lava lamp

Lava lamp is a WebGL effect: raymarched 3D metaballs; heat drives buoyancy. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add lava-lamp.

A chrome-and-glass lava lamp glows in a dim room: wax swells on the bulb, necks off the pool, rises slowly, cools at the top and sinks, merging and pinching as it goes.

Raymarched in one shader: the wax is 3D metaballs joined by a smooth minimum, and each blob's heat sets its buoyancy; light refracts through the glass and the wax glows where it is thin.

Settings: --blobs 8 (2 to 14, step 1; Blobs); --speed 0.5 (0.1 to 2, step 0.05; Speed).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 14.8 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/lava-lamp.html

### Fire & smoke

Fire & smoke is a WebGL effect: combustion simulated: fuel burns out, gas glows as a blackbody. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add fire-smoke.

A campfire at night burning on stacked logs: flames lick up from the wood and the coals, the logs’ charred skin glows orange in its cracks, and smoke and sparks rise.

Fuel gas from the hot wood burns at a fixed rate, so flame tips are where it runs out; everything hot glows by Planck’s law, and the char is Voronoi blocks lit by the fire.

Settings: --heat 1 (0.2 to 2, step 0.05; Heat); --cooling 0.95 (0.85 to 0.99, step 0.005; Heat persistence); --curl 22 (0 to 50, step 1; Curl).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 34.2 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/fire-smoke.html

### Lava flow

Lava flow is a WebGL effect: lava simulated on an eroded volcano, lit by blackbody light. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add lava-flow.

A volcano at dusk: red-hot lava pours from the crater and runs down the gullies in glowing channels, dark rafts of crust drifting on it, its light on the slopes and plume.

A thickness-and-heat simulation runs on the raymarched mountain; the vent surges, crust plates set at their own age and ride the flow, and colour is Planck’s law.

Settings: --flow 1 (0.5 to 1.6, step 0.05; Flow); --cooling 1 (0.4 to 2.5, step 0.1; Cooling); --speed 1 (0.5 to 1.5, step 0.1; Speed).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 30.3 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/lava-flow.html

### Ferrofluid

Ferrofluid is a WebGL effect: rosensweig needles on a block magnet: concave cones on a hex lattice, raymarched as black mirrors. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add ferrofluid.

Black, mirror-glossy oil lies in a puddle on a studio table, climbs a square nickel magnet and bristles into a crown of fine needles, tallest along its edges; move the pointer to slide the magnet through the puddle (it drags the oil along), and click or tap to switch it off and watch the needles melt.

Raymarched distance field: the puddle smooth-unioned with a film on the block and concave cones on a hexagonal lattice (each sample visits only its nearest lattice point and six neighbours), shaded only by studio reflections.

Settings: --spikes 260 (80 to 500, step 10; Spikes); --strength 1 (0 to 2, step 0.05; Magnet strength); --magnet 0 (0 to 1, step 1; Magnet).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 22.5 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/ferrofluid.html

### Paper marbling

Paper marbling is a WebGL effect: backward lookup through comb and swirl warps; paint never smears. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add marbling.

Bands of paint are combed and swirled like marbled paper; the pointer drags the stylus.

Each pixel traces backward through the comb waves and stylus swirl to find its paint band, so the backward lookup never smears.

Settings: --comb 1 (0 to 2, step 0.05; Comb); --swirl 1 (0 to 2, step 0.05; Swirl).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 3.8 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/marbling.html

### Rain on glass

Rain on glass is a Canvas effect: each drop is a lens showing a sharp, flipped background. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add raindrops-glass.

Raindrops bead and slide down a window over a blurred city, each showing a sharp flipped copy.

Each drop samples the sharp scene flipped and shrunk, as a tiny lens; heavy drops slide in fits, swallow small beads and leave trails.

Settings: --rain 1 (0.2 to 3, step 0.1; Rain); --size 1 (0.5 to 2, step 0.05; Drop size).

### Dripping text

Dripping text is a Canvas effect: gooey blur-and-threshold filter: drips merge with letters, necks snap. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add dripping-text.

Drops swell under the letters, stretch, snap off and collect in a puddle.

Drops start at the text’s bottom edges; a blur followed by a hard alpha threshold fuses drop and letter into one liquid outline.

Settings: --drips 14 (4 to 30, step 1; Drips); --viscosity 1 (0.4 to 3, step 0.05; Viscosity).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 3.8 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/dripping-text.html

### Liquid mercury

Liquid mercury is a WebGL effect: metaball beads that merge, split and mirror an environment. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add mercury.

Beads of mercury roll, merge on contact and split when you move fast through them.

Beads sum into one metaball field turned into a height and normal in the shader; the normal reflects a studio, and merging conserves area and momentum.

Settings: --beads 14 (4 to 22, step 1; Starting beads); --cohesion 1 (0 to 2, step 0.05; Cohesion); --tilt 1 (0 to 2, step 0.05; Tray tilt).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 11.3 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/mercury.html

### Kelvin–Helmholtz clouds

Kelvin–Helmholtz clouds is a WebGL effect: shear-layer fluid sim rolls up Kelvin–Helmholtz billows by itself. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add billow-clouds.

At sunset a cloud sheet rolls up into a row of breaking waves, then dissolves into turbulence.

A GPU fluid with shear, buoyancy, vorticity confinement and a pressure solve grows Kelvin–Helmholtz billows; the dye is lit by a march toward the sun.

Settings: --shear 1 (0.6 to 1.5, step 0.05; Shear); --curl 1 (0 to 3, step 0.1; Curl); --speed 1 (0.5 to 1.5, step 0.1; Speed).

### Paint swirl

Paint swirl is a WebGL effect: colour advected around vortices; palette snapping keeps bands crisp. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add paint-swirl.

Rings of paint pour from two spouts and wind into crisp spirals; circle the pointer to stir.

Semi-Lagrangian advection through Lamb–Oseen vortices with clamped Catmull-Rom sampling; nudging each pixel toward the nearest paint colour keeps bands crisp.

Settings: --vortices 4 (1 to 6, step 1; Vortices); --strength 1 (0 to 2.5, step 0.05; Swirl strength); --pour 1 (0 to 2, step 0.05; Pour).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 10.2 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/paint-swirl.html

### SPH water tank

SPH water tank is a WebGL effect: real SPH particles, splatted into one surface and traced through glass. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add sph-water.

Water sloshes in a rocking glass tank, climbing the walls, foaming and casting caustics; the pointer tilts it.

SPH with double density relaxation; particles splat into a float field, and each pixel traces it in perspective for absorption, meniscus, Fresnel surface and caustics.

Settings: --particles 1600 (800 to 2800, step 100; Particles); --slosh 1 (0 to 1.5, step 0.05; Slosh).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 26.8 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/sph-water.html

### Open ocean

Open ocean is a WebGL effect: FFT ocean from a JONSWAP spectrum with a broad directional spread; foam where the surface folds. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add ocean.

A grey, windy open sea under an overcast sky: four GPU FFTs turn a JONSWAP wave spectrum with a broad directional spread into Gerstner waves each frame, and foam forms and streaks downwind where the surface folds.

Wind sets wave height and how often whitecaps break, chop sharpens the crests, sun is the height of the hidden sun behind the clouds; the pointer moves its bright patch along the horizon.

Settings: --wind 10 (5 to 13, step 0.5; Wind (m/s)); --chop 1.6 (0.6 to 1.9, step 0.05; Choppiness); --sun 10 (1 to 20, step 0.5; Sun height (°)).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 35.5 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/ocean.html

### Honey pour

Honey pour is a WebGL effect: liquid-rope coiling: stacked tube loops sink into a thin-film mound. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add honey-coil.

Each fresh loop is a tube resting on the loop beneath; it sinks, melts into a height field and spreads by the thin-film equation.

Flow sets the thread thickness, loops the coils per second, spread how fast the mound slumps; drag the pointer to stitch trails of loops.

Settings: --flow 1 (0.5 to 1.5, step 0.05; Flow); --loops 1.5 (0.8 to 2.5, step 0.1; Loops per second); --spread 1 (0.6 to 2.5, step 0.05; Spread).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 36.3 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/honey-coil.html

## Shaders & glitch

### CRT monitor

CRT monitor is a WebGL effect: simulated electron beam, phosphor decay and aperture-grille stripes. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add crt-monitor.

An old CRT switches on, boots, plays Breakout by itself and collapses to a dot.

A 320×240 canvas with phosphor persistence feeds a tube pass that curves the glass, draws brightness-width beam lines and box-filtered RGB stripes.

Settings: --curve 1 (0 to 2.5, step 0.05; Curvature); --glow 1 (0 to 2.5, step 0.05; Glow); --mask 1 (0 to 1.5, step 0.05; Phosphor mask).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 19.8 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/crt-monitor.html

### CMYK halftone

CMYK halftone is a WebGL effect: rotated dot screens (C15° M75° Y0° K45°) printed in light. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add cmyk-halftone.

Drifting colour orbs print as rotated halftone dot screens forming rosettes; the cursor makes dots bloom.

Each separation is a grid at its classic angle; every pixel finds its cell, samples at the centre and draws one dot sized to the ink coverage.

Settings: --dot 10 (4 to 20, step 0.5; Dot pitch (px)); --speed 1 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Speed); --bloom 1 (0 to 2, step 0.05; Pointer bloom).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 7.6 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/cmyk-halftone.html

### Reaction–diffusion

Reaction–diffusion is a WebGL effect: gray–Scott: two chemicals, feed and kill. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add reaction-diffusion.

Spots, stripes and coral patterns grow and shift across the surface.

A Gray-Scott-style reaction–diffusion on the GPU, several steps per frame; two chemicals spread at different rates and the feed and kill rates set the pattern.

Settings: --feed 0.037 (0.025 to 0.05, step 0.001; Feed); --kill 0.06 (0.058 to 0.0655, step 0.0005; Kill).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 5.7 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/reaction-diffusion.html

### Guilloche spirograph

Guilloche spirograph is a Canvas effect: a hypotrochoid, drawn as a seven-line ribbon. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add guilloche.

Engraved banknote-style rosettes of fine looping lines.

Hypotrochoids, a point on a small circle rolling inside a big one, closing for whole-number ratios; seven slightly offset copies give the engraved look.

Settings: --R 7 (3 to 12, step 1; Big circle); --r 4 (1 to 9, step 1; Small circle); --d 5.2 (1 to 9, step 0.1; Pen offset); --lines 7 (1 to 12, step 1; Lines).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 2.4 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/guilloche.html

### RGB-split glitch

RGB-split glitch is a Canvas effect: shift the colour channels, displace slices. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add rgb-glitch.

A picture splits into colour channels while slices jump sideways in random bursts.

Each colour channel is drawn separately with additive blending and offset; during unpredictable bursts horizontal slices shift and scanlines jitter.

Settings: --intensity 1 (0 to 2, step 0.05; Intensity); --rate 0.8 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Bursts / second).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 3.2 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/rgb-glitch.html

### Domain-warped marble

Domain-warped marble is a WebGL effect: noise sampled at noise-warped coordinates: f(p + g(p + h(p))). One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add domain-warp.

Smoky marbled filaments fold and flow endlessly.

Domain warping: noise read at a point pushed by noise read at a pushed point; the intermediate push vectors pick colours so the dye follows the folds.

Settings: --warp 1 (0 to 2, step 0.05; Warp); --speed 1 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Speed).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 3.8 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/domain-warp.html

### Truchet flow

Truchet flow is a WebGL effect: random quarter-arc tiles that always connect, checkerboard flow. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add truchet.

Dashes flow along winding paths that reroute as tiles occasionally turn.

Truchet tiles of two quarter-circle arcs in random orientations; flipping flow direction on a checkerboard keeps dashes continuous between tiles.

Settings: --tiles 9 (3 to 20, step 1; Tiles across); --flow 1 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Flow speed).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 4.0 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/truchet.html

### Kaleidoscope

Kaleidoscope is a WebGL effect: polar angle wrapped into one mirrored wedge. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add kaleidoscope.

A slowly turning kaleidoscope of glass chips with a warm light leak.

Polar coordinates with the angle wrapped into one wedge and mirrored at its edges; the wedge holds moving Voronoi cells, with per-channel scale for colour fringes.

Settings: --mirrors 8 (3 to 16, step 1; Mirrors); --zoom 1 (0.5 to 2.5, step 0.05; Zoom).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 4.2 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/kaleidoscope.html

### Ordered dither

Ordered dither is a WebGL effect: ordered dithering against an 8×8 Bayer threshold matrix. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add dither.

A small 3D scene rendered in two chunky ink tones that read as smooth grey.

Each pixel’s brightness is compared with a threshold from an 8×8 Bayer matrix; rendering at low resolution and upscaling without smoothing keeps the grid crisp.

Settings: --pixel 2 (1 to 6, step 1; Pixel size); --tones 2 (2 to 6, step 1; Tones).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 5.3 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/dither.html

### Pen sketch

Pen sketch is a WebGL effect: hatching layered by lighting; outlines from depth and normal jumps. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add pen-sketch.

Plaster solids on a turntable drawn in boiling blue-black ink with hatching that deepens into shadow.

A G-buffer pass stores light, depth and normal; the pen pass draws outlines at jumps and layers hatching directions by darkness, redrawn on twos.

Settings: --density 1 (0.5 to 2, step 0.05; Hatch density); --boil 8 (1 to 24, step 1; Boils / second); --speed 1 (0 to 3, step 0.1; Turntable speed).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 11.7 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/pen-sketch.html

### ASCII render

ASCII render is a WebGL effect: brightness picks a glyph, edges pick - / | \ by direction. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add ascii-render.

A Menger sponge turns over a floor, drawn only in amber characters.

Raymarched per character cell; edge cells pick - / | \ from a Sobel structure tensor, and others pick glyphs from a brightness ramp in a pre-drawn atlas.

Settings: --cell 7 (5 to 16, step 1; Cell width (px)); --spin 1 (0 to 3, step 0.1; Spin); --edges 1 (0.3 to 3, step 0.1; Edge sensitivity).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 11.9 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/ascii-render.html

### Pixel sort

Pixel sort is a WebGL effect: GPU odd-even transposition sort within bright runs per column. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add pixel-sort.

A stormy sunset melts as bright sky pours down in sorted streaks, then drains away.

Runs of above-threshold pixels in each column are sorted by brightness with odd-even transposition, ten passes a frame, so the sort is visible.

Settings: --threshold 0.42 (0.15 to 0.85, step 0.01; Threshold); --passes 10 (1 to 40, step 1; Sort passes / frame); --speed 1 (0.2 to 3, step 0.1; Speed).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 11.5 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/pixel-sort.html

### Hyperbolic tiling

Hyperbolic tiling is a WebGL effect: fold pixels into one triangle by reflections; glide by Möbius map. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add hyperbolic-tiling.

A woven star pattern of seven-sided tiles streams endlessly toward the rim of a Poincaré disk.

Each pixel is folded into one fundamental triangle by rotations, mirrors and circle inversions; the flip count decides over-under weaving at crossings.

Settings: --p 7 (3 to 10, step 1; Sides per tile); --q 3 (3 to 8, step 1; Tiles per corner); --speed 1 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Speed).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 10.7 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/hyperbolic-tiling.html

### Stained glass

Stained glass is a WebGL effect: trace light back to a glass function: coloured pools and dusty shafts. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add stained-glass.

Sun pours through a row of leaded windows set deep in a stone nave: coloured shafts in the dusty air, and pools on the polished flagstones that drift as it moves.

The window is a function that returns glass colour or lead; the floor and every step of a march through the air look it up along the sunlight. Move across to move the sun.

Settings: --dust 1 (0 to 2, step 0.05; Dust); --sun 1 (0.3 to 2, step 0.05; Sun); --speed 1 (0 to 3, step 0.1; Speed).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 18.5 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/stained-glass.html


## Generative & math

### Op-art moiré

Op-art moiré is a WebGL effect: two fine ring gratings beat into broad, fast-moving moiré fringes. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add op-art-moire.

Two sets of fine rings overlap into sweeping moiré fringes; the pointer steers one centre.

Each ring set is a 50% stripe of distance antialiased with fwidth; the product of the two, lit hard, makes bright coincidences and dark interleaves.

Settings: --rings 52 (16 to 90, step 1; Rings); --spread 0.16 (0.02 to 0.5, step 0.01; Centre spread); --speed 1 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Speed).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 4.5 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/op-art-moire.html

### Bauhaus composition

Bauhaus composition is a Canvas effect: primary tiles that re-compose themselves through staggered, eased tweens. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add bauhaus.

A Bauhaus poster of coloured tiles where a third of the figures change in a ripple.

Each change is a quarter turn, a shrink-and-grow or a ground wipe, with start times staggered 70 ms apart; five colours keep every frame on-grid.

Settings: --rows 4 (2 to 8, step 1; Rows); --tempo 1 (0.25 to 3, step 0.05; Tempo); --change 0.3 (0.05 to 1, step 0.05; Share that changes).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 5.9 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/bauhaus.html

### Memphis pattern

Memphis pattern is a Canvas effect: jittered-grid confetti of Memphis shapes, wrapping seamlessly in three parallax layers. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add memphis.

Memphis squiggles, zigzags and dots drift over a dark ground; the pointer shifts three depth layers.

Shapes are dealt one per jittered grid cell so they never clump, and positions wrap by modulo over a span wider than the stage.

Settings: --density 1 (0.4 to 2.5, step 0.05; Density); --speed 1 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Speed); --stroke 4 (1.5 to 8, step 0.5; Stroke (px)).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 5.5 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/memphis.html

### Phyllotaxis

Phyllotaxis is a Canvas effect: seeds at the golden angle, radius ∝ √age: why 137.5° packs perfectly. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add phyllotaxis.

Seeds grow outward in a sunflower head as the angle sways around 137.508°, opening spokes. Left to right turns the angle from 130.5° to 144.5°, catching at 137.508°.

Seed j sits at angle j·α and radius c·√(age), keeping constant area per seed; colouring by index mod 21 traces each spiral arm.

Settings: --angle 137.508 (130 to 145, step 0.001; Angle (°)); --sweep 0.6 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Sweep (±°)); --dots 1500 (300 to 3000, step 50; Seeds).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 5.0 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/phyllotaxis.html

### Rose curve

Rose curve is a Canvas effect: r = cos(kθ) traced by a comet pen, k gliding between fractions. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add rose-curve.

A glowing pen traces a polar rose, holds it, then morphs into the next. The pointer picks the ratio n/d: across for n, down for d.

With k = n/d the curve closes after d·π turns when n·d is odd and 2d·π otherwise; three lighter-blended strokes of one path give the glow.

Settings: --speed 1 (0.2 to 3, step 0.05; Speed); --glow 1 (0 to 2.5, step 0.05; Glow); --width 1.8 (0.6 to 4, step 0.1; Line width).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 7.3 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/rose-curve.html

### Superformula

Superformula is a Canvas effect: Gielis superformula outlines blended radius by radius, echoed into ribbons. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add superformula.

A star morphs into a square, gear, triangle and flower, trailing fading nested echoes. The pointer sets symmetry and sharpness, from spiky star to round flower.

Gielis’s superformula sampled at 720 angles and normalised; the morph eases radius by radius, and each echo is an earlier frame drawn slightly smaller.

Settings: --echoes 22 (1 to 40, step 1; Echoes); --speed 1 (0.2 to 3, step 0.05; Speed); --hold 1.6 (0.2 to 5, step 0.1; Hold (s)).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 7.0 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/superformula.html

### Hex wave

Hex wave is a Canvas effect: honeycomb prisms lifted by summed travelling rings and a swell. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add hex-wave.

Rings of raised, glowing hex prisms spread over a slow swell; click or move to drop rings.

Each cell sums Gaussian ring bumps by its distance, passed through tanh to set lift and colour; painting rows top to bottom gives the occlusion.

Settings: --cell 16 (8 to 32, step 1; Cell (px)); --speed 1 (0.2 to 3, step 0.05; Speed); --lift 1 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Lift).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 4.8 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/hex-wave.html

### Wave lines

Wave lines is a Canvas effect: harmonics phase-shifted line to line; hidden-line ridges drift diagonally. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add wave-lines.

A stack of hairlines rises into ridges that travel diagonally down and flatten again. The pointer pinches the lines up into a glowing peak.

Each line sums sine harmonics whose phase steps per line at different rates; filling below each line before stroking hides the ridges behind.

Settings: --lines 46 (10 to 90, step 1; Lines); --harmonics 4 (1 to 5, step 1; Harmonics); --speed 1 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Speed); --height 1 (0.2 to 2.5, step 0.05; Height).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 6.2 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/wave-lines.html

### Starburst

Starburst is a Canvas effect: counter-rotating ray fans and zooming rings, combined with a difference blend. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add starburst.

A sunburst of rays spins, flickers and streams outward through bands of colour. The pointer moves a second ray fan, and the two cross into moiré arcs.

Two counter-rotating wedge fans and log-spaced rings combined with difference blending; constant-ratio ring spacing makes the outward motion an endless zoom.

Settings: --rays 18 (4 to 48, step 1; Rays); --speed 1 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Speed); --rings 1 (0 to 1, step 0.05; Rings).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 4.7 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/starburst.html

### Log spiral

Log spiral is a WebGL effect: rotating log spirals look like an endless zoom inward. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add spiral.

Gold and blue spirals weave a diamond lattice that pours endlessly into a glowing centre. The pointer is a second pole the spirals stream out of.

In log-polar space a log spiral is a straight line, so each family is a stripe of N·θ + k·log r, drawn as fwidth hairlines.

Settings: --arms 21 (5 to 40, step 1; Arms); --twist 1 (0 to 2, step 0.05; Twist); --speed 1 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Speed).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 6.4 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/spiral.html

### Woven tartan

Woven tartan is a WebGL effect: real 2/2 twill per pixel: a mirrored sett on warp and weft. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add tartan.

A close-up of woven tartan slides diagonally, every thread and twill rib visible.

One mirrored sett in a 1-pixel texture serves warp and weft; a 2/2 twill rule, warp on top where (i + j) mod 4 < 2, picks the visible thread.

Settings: --thread 3 (1.5 to 10, step 0.5; Thread (px)); --speed 1 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Speed); --relief 1 (0 to 1, step 0.05; Yarn relief).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 5.8 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/tartan.html

### Clifford attractor

Clifford attractor is a WebGL effect: a million GPU orbits a frame into a log-tone-mapped density buffer. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add clifford-attractor.

A silky self-crossing ribbon of light reshapes as its four parameters drift. Pointer x and y set two coefficients, reshaping the attractor under your hand.

Each vertex iterates the Clifford map 24 times from a hashed gl_VertexID start, then splats additively into a decaying half-float buffer mapped by log(1 + k·n).

Settings: --points 1 (0.1 to 3, step 0.1; Points (millions/frame)); --drift 1 (0 to 4, step 0.05; Drift); --exposure 1 (0.2 to 4, step 0.05; Exposure).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 9.9 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/clifford-attractor.html

### Barnsley fern

Barnsley fern is a Canvas effect: chaos game with four affine maps, shaded by hit count. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add barnsley-fern.

A fern assembles from scattered dots, outline first, then leaflets and veins. The pointer is wind: the fern leans and curls toward it.

The chaos game with four weighted affine maps plotted into a per-pixel hit counter that indexes a colour ramp; points per frame grow exponentially.

Settings: --rate 1 (0.2 to 5, step 0.1; Build rate); --hold 4 (0.5 to 10, step 0.5; Hold (s)); --glow 1 (0.3 to 3, step 0.1; Glow).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 7.7 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/barnsley-fern.html

### Chaos game

Chaos game is a Canvas effect: random jumps toward corners converge on the Sierpinski triangle. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add sierpinski.

A point jumping halfway to random corners draws a Sierpinski triangle in nested colours. The pointer pulls the nearest corner, and the figure re-forms around it.

The chaos game with per-pixel hit counts and colour sums; each hit is tinted by the last two corners, the point’s address, so every sub-copy gets its hue.

Settings: --sides 3 (3 to 9, step 1; Sides); --ratio 0.5 (0.2 to 0.9, step 0.01; Jump ratio); --rate 1 (0.2 to 5, step 0.1; Speed).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 9.4 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/sierpinski.html

### Dragon curve

Dragon curve is a Canvas effect: each fold copies the curve and swings it open by 90°. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add dragon-curve.

A Heighway dragon unfolds one crease at a time to 8,192 segments, then folds back. Left to right opens every crease from 60° to 150°, catching at 90°.

Each step appends the existing points in reverse, rotated about the last point by a fold angle eased from 0 to 90°, while the view counter-rotates.

Settings: --folds 13 (1 to 16, step 1; Folds); --angle 90 (30 to 150, step 1; Fold angle (°)); --speed 1 (0.2 to 3, step 0.05; Speed).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 6.3 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/dragon-curve.html

### Dot-matrix wave

Dot-matrix wave is a WebGL effect: one disc per cell, sized and coloured by rolling waves. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add dot-matrix-wave.

A grid of dots breathes in rolling bands; the cursor raises a hot dome with a moat.

Each pixel finds its cell, samples a height field of plane and circular waves at the centre, and draws one anti-aliased disc sized and coloured by it.

Settings: --cells 38 (16 to 80, step 1; Dots per column); --amp 1 (0 to 1.5, step 0.05; Wave strength); --speed 1 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Speed).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 6.8 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/dot-matrix-wave.html

### Metaballs

Metaballs is a WebGL effect: summed inverse-square fields, thresholded into one surface. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add metaballs.

Glossy blobs drift and flow into one another with smooth necks; the cursor is a blob too.

Each blob adds r² / d² to a field with the surface at 1; the field’s exact gradient lights each pixel and anti-aliases the rim.

Settings: --count 7 (2 to 12, step 1; Blobs); --speed 1 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Speed); --gloss 1 (0 to 2, step 0.05; Gloss).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 7.0 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/metaballs.html

### Aurora curtains

Aurora curtains is a WebGL effect: folded light curtains: bright hems, stretched-noise rays, altitude colour. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add aurora-ribbons.

Green aurora curtains pleat and drift across a starry sky, shimmering into violet above. The pointer lifts the nearest curtain into a bright fold.

Each curtain hangs from a noise curve bent by sines, brighter where the bend’s slope nears zero (edge-on); light fades exponentially with height.

Settings: --layers 3 (1 to 5, step 1; Curtains); --speed 1 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Speed); --rays 1 (0 to 2, step 0.05; Rays).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 8.5 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/aurora-ribbons.html

### Ripple grid

Ripple grid is a WebGL effect: damped ring waves displace the coordinates a grid is drawn in. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add ripple-grid.

A fine grid floats like graph paper on water, rings spreading from clicks and movement.

Ripple wave trains’ radial displacements are summed per pixel and the grid drawn at the displaced spot with screen-space derivatives for one-pixel lines.

Settings: --cells 36 (12 to 80, step 1; Grid lines); --speed 1 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Speed); --depth 1 (0 to 2, step 0.05; Ripple depth).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 7.7 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/ripple-grid.html

### Voronoi cells

Voronoi cells is a WebGL effect: nearest and second-nearest seed distances; walls where F2 − F1 ≈ 0. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add voronoi-cells.

A glass mosaic of drifting cells with glowing walls that slide and swap partners. The pointer is one more seed, pushing its neighbours aside.

Each pixel checks the 3 × 3 neighbouring seeds for F1 and F2; dividing F2 − F1 by its exact gradient keeps the walls an even pixel width.

Settings: --scale 5 (2 to 14, step 0.5; Cells across); --speed 1 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Speed); --glow 1 (0 to 2, step 0.05; Glow).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 7.7 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/voronoi-cells.html

### Quasicrystal

Quasicrystal is a WebGL effect: n rotated plane waves summed: ordered, symmetric, never repeating. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add quasicrystal.

Gold rings and five-pointed rosettes bloom outward in a pattern that never repeats. The pointer shifts the waves’ phases, so rosettes melt and re-form.

Five stripe waves at k · 36° are summed, giving quasi-periodic interference; shifting all phases together streams it outward, and a triangle wave folds it into rings.

Settings: --waves 5 (3 to 13, step 1; Waves (symmetry)); --scale 70 (20 to 140, step 1; Frequency); --speed 1 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Speed).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 6.2 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/quasicrystal.html

### Topographic contours

Topographic contours is a WebGL effect: isolines of morphing noise terrain, made pixel-exact with fwidth. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add topographic.

Contour lines of a slowly shifting landscape crowd on slopes and close into rings on peaks. The pointer raises a hill the contours ring around; press to sink a pit.

Domain-warped noise gives the height; the distance to the nearest contour, divided by fwidth, is measured in pixels, so every line stays equally crisp on steep and gentle ground.

Settings: --levels 22 (6 to 48, step 1; Contour levels); --scale 1.6 (0.5 to 4, step 0.1; Terrain scale); --speed 1 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Speed).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 7.1 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/topographic.html

### Wave interference

Wave interference is a WebGL effect: point sources summed as complex waves; fixed fringes, travelling crests. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add interference.

Two ripple sources cross into bright bands and black nodal lines; move the cursor to drag one source.

Per pixel, each source adds a complex number with phase k · distance and amplitude 1/√distance; the sum’s size gives the fixed fringes, its rotated real part the live wave.

Settings: --sources 2 (2 to 5, step 1; Sources); --waves 16 (4 to 40, step 1; Waves per height); --speed 1 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Speed).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 6.3 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/interference.html

### Plasma

Plasma is a WebGL effect: four sines summed, through a dark-light-dark ramp, not a rainbow. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add plasma.

Neon lobes swell, merge and fold, warm coral on one side and ice blue on the other. The rings spread out from the pointer.

The demoscene recipe: per pixel, sum sines along x, y, a diagonal and a circle; a cosine maps the sum into a dark-light-dark ramp, giving each lobe a lit rim.

Settings: --scale 1.3 (0.4 to 3, step 0.05; Scale); --speed 1 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Speed); --bands 1 (0 to 2, step 0.05; Sheen bands).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 6.6 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/plasma.html

### Heatmap

Heatmap is a WebGL effect: a drifting field, sampled per cell, through a perceptual heat palette. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add heatmap.

A grid of rounded cells glows from black through crimson to pale yellow as hot spots drift. The pointer leaves heat that spreads and slowly cools.

Domain-warped noise plus wandering Gaussians is sampled at each cell’s centre and mapped through an inferno-like palette whose brightness rises evenly; cells are SDF rounded squares.

Settings: --rows 30 (8 to 60, step 1; Rows); --scale 1.2 (0.4 to 3, step 0.05; Field scale); --speed 1 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Speed).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 8.3 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/heatmap.html

### Julia set

Julia set is a WebGL effect: z → z² + c, with c gliding along the Mandelbrot edge. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add julia-set.

A glowing fractal morphs endlessly: fat lobes melt into spirals, then lace and dust, and back. Move the pointer to steer c yourself.

Each pixel iterates z → z² + c while c travels along the Mandelbrot cardioid’s edge; a distance estimate in pixels keeps the finest filaments one pixel sharp.

Settings: --speed 1 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Speed); --detail 1 (0.5 to 3, step 0.1; Iterations ×).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 8.1 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/julia-set.html

### Wave function collapse

Wave function collapse is a Canvas effect: collapse the least certain cell, then propagate what its neighbours may be. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add wave-collapse.

An island map writes itself: unsolved cells hold every terrain at once until the solver picks one, and coastlines, beaches and ridges grow out from there. Press and drag to dissolve a patch and watch it regrow.

Neighbours may differ by one terrain step at most. The cell with the lowest entropy collapses, its neighbours lose what they can no longer be, and a contradiction is repaired by dissolving the patch around it.

Settings: --cell 22 (14 to 34, step 1; Cell size); --speed 5 (1 to 20, step 1; Cells per frame); --land 1 (0.5 to 1.6, step 0.05; Land).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 14.7 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/wave-collapse.html


## Simulation

### Brian’s Brain

Brian’s Brain is a Canvas effect: three-state cellular automaton: fire, refractory, off; gliders everywhere. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add brians-brain.

Spaceships streak across a grid, crash and spawn new ones, trailing cooling blue tails; drag to paint cells.

A cell fires when exactly two of its eight neighbours fire, then must die and rest a step; that forced rest keeps everything moving.

Settings: --cell 6 (3 to 12, step 1; Cell size); --rate 18 (2 to 40, step 1; Generations / s); --trail 0.88 (0 to 0.97, step 0.01; Afterglow).

### Langton’s ant

Langton’s ant is a Canvas effect: turn right on empty, left on filled, flip, step: then a highway. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add langtons-ant.

One ant scribbles chaos for about ten thousand steps, then builds a straight diagonal highway.

Turn right on an empty cell, left on a filled one, flip it, step forward; the chaos always falls into a 104-step cycle. Cells are coloured by when last touched.

Settings: --speed 120 (1 to 1000, step 1; Steps / frame); --cell 5 (2 to 10, step 1; Cell size).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 4.6 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/langtons-ant.html

### Falling sand

Falling sand is a Canvas effect: cellular automaton: grains fall, slide diagonally, water spreads sideways. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add falling-sand.

Fine desert sand pours from the cursor, piles on the ledges and settles into layered dunes; now and then a burst of water runs down, pools in the hollows and darkens the sand it soaks.

A grid of grains scanned bottom-up: each falls, gaining speed, or slides diagonally, water also spreads sideways and soaks in, and 32-cell chunks where nothing moved go to sleep.

Settings: --rate 200 (40 to 600, step 10; Pour rate); --water 0.08 (0 to 0.5, step 0.02; Water share); --cell 1.5 (1 to 4, step 0.5; Grain size).

### Doom fire

Doom fire is a Canvas effect: the PlayStation Doom fire: copy heat up, jitter sideways, cool randomly. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add doom-fire.

A wall of chunky pixel fire sways, dies down and roars back; drag to add heat anywhere.

Heat values 0–36 rise from a hot bottom row: each cell copies upward, shifted sideways and cooled by one shared random number, then a 37-colour ramp turns it into flame.

### Water ripples

Water ripples is a WebGL effect: height-field wave equation on the GPU, refracting a grid beneath. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add water-ripple.

Now and then a drop falls into clear water and sends a slow ring across it, bending the grid beneath; drag for a wake, click for a big drop.

The wave equation on two ping-pong float textures: each cell moves toward its neighbours’ average (slower than the fastest stable rate, so rings can be followed) minus its previous height, damped; the slope refracts the grid and curvature adds caustics.

Settings: --damping 0.985 (0.95 to 0.998, step 0.001; Damping); --refraction 1 (0 to 3, step 0.05; Refraction); --rain 1 (0 to 4, step 0.1; Rain); --speed 0.55 (0.2 to 1, step 0.05; Ripple speed).
Renderer: WebGL. Size: 9.4 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/water-ripple.html

### Double pendulums

Double pendulums is a Canvas effect: chaos: pendulums a fraction of a milliradian apart diverge completely. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add double-pendulum.

Nine double pendulums swing as one white trace, then suddenly fan out into colours that never agree again. The pointer holds the pivot, so the pendulums swing from your hand.

They start a fraction of a milliradian apart and run Runge–Kutta 4 on the full equations; chaos doubles the gap each swing. Additive trails make the shared trace white.

Settings: --count 9 (2 to 16, step 1; Pendulums); --spread 0.2 (0.01 to 5, step 0.01; Start spread (mrad)); --speed 1 (0.1 to 3, step 0.05; Speed).
Renderer: Canvas 2D. Size: 7.4 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/double-pendulum.html

### N-body orbits

N-body orbits is a Canvas effect: every body pulls every other; leapfrog integration keeps orbits closed. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add orbits.

Planets circle twin suns in slowly turning rosettes while comets swing through; click to drop a planet.

Softened inverse-square gravity between every pair, stepped with leapfrog (half kick, drift, half kick), which is symplectic, so orbits stay closed; the binary’s tug makes them precess.

Settings: --planets 6 (1 to 10, step 1; Planets); --speed 1 (0.1 to 3, step 0.05; Speed); --trail 900 (50 to 1500, step 10; Trail length).

### Vortex drain

Vortex drain is a Canvas effect: lamb–Oseen vortex plus inflow; differential rotation winds colour into arms. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add vortex.

Thousands of streaks spiral into a drain that follows the cursor, their colours wound into spiral arms.

A Lamb–Oseen vortex: tangential swirl falling off as 1/r outside a smooth core and a weak inward pull; particles keep their birth sector’s colour, which inner rings shear into spirals.

Settings: --count 9000 (1000 to 20000, step 500; Particles); --swirl 1 (0.2 to 3, step 0.05; Swirl); --pull 0.3 (0 to 1.5, step 0.05; Pull).

### Plexus

Plexus is a Canvas effect: drifting points linked by distance-faded lines, found through a grid. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add plexus.

Drifting points knit a mesh of fine lines, and the cursor gathers the nearest into warm links.

Points link to neighbours within a set distance, fading with length, found through a uniform grid one link wide; lines are batched into a few opacity buckets, one path each.

### Lenia

Lenia is a WebGL effect: ring-kernel convolution and a growth bump: Chan’s Lenia, four species. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add lenia.

Real creatures from Bert Chan’s Lenia catalogue glide, spin, collide and heal in a drop under a fluorescence microscope; move to focus, drag to wound.

Each cell averages its neighbours through a soft ring and grows or fades by a bell curve. Speed sets steps per frame; Population sets how many live.

### Differential growth

Differential growth is a WebGL effect: repel, align, split stretched edges: a growing line folds to fit. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add diff-growth.

A fine ink line grows longer than its paper allows and folds outward into a branching maze, with nested contours inside; the ink runs from deep blue at the old centre to vermilion at the newest edge.

Nodes push away others in reach, ease toward their neighbours’ midpoint and split stretched edges. Growth sets how often roomy nodes split; Fold spacing sets fold width.

### Snowflake growth

Vapour diffuses on a hex lattice; edge sites freeze when their liquid layer is thick enough, and corners outgrow faces into branches.

Each loop grows a different crystal from four parameter sets; size zooms the microscope, speed sets how fast it grows.

### Mud cracks

Mud cracks is a Canvas effect: warped Voronoi walls tear open as the drying front passes. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add mud-cracks.

Wet, glossy clay dries unevenly and tears into curled plates, the cracks widening as it shrinks; then rain soaks it and the cracks close. Press and drag to wet a patch.

Even shrinkage breaks clay into polygons, so the network is a noise-warped Voronoi diagram; each wall tears from its middle out when its spot dries, and a distance transform shades the gaps and curled rims.

### Digital rain

Columns of mirrored katakana and digits pour down, each led by a white head and fading green tail.

Every glyph is drawn once with fillText into an atlas at device resolution and stamped with drawImage, so thousands per frame stay crisp and cheap.

### Warp starfield

Warp starfield is a Canvas effect: perspective-projected stars whose streak length grows with speed. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add starfield-warp.

Stars rush from a vanishing point, dots at cruise and long streaks at warp; the pointer steers.

Each 3D star is drawn as a line from its last projected position (x/z, y/z) to its current one, so speed lengthens streaks for free; lines are batched by colour.

### Oscilloscope

Oscilloscope is a Canvas effect: x-Y Lissajous beam with speed-dependent brightness and phosphor afterglow. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add oscilloscope.

A green CRT trace draws drifting Lissajous figures over a graticule, leaving a fading phosphor afterglow. Left–right picks the frequency ratio, up–down the phase.

Two sine generators drive x and y; each segment’s brightness is inverse to its length, as with a real beam, and each frame only partly fades the last.

### Rotozoom

Rotozoom is a WebGL effect: one texture lookup through a rotating, breathing scale matrix. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add rotozoom.

A XOR pattern of nested squares spins and zooms in and out across the screen.

Each pixel’s coordinates go through a rotation-and-scale matrix that changes per frame, then look up a 256×256 x ^ y texture; mipmaps stop shimmer when zoomed out.

## Basics

### Fade & scale in

Fade & scale in is a DOM effect: cards rise from 94% scale, never from zero. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add fade-scale.

Tap a shop filter and the product cards leave quickly, then the new ones rise in turn.

Each card enters from 94% scale and transparent with a hard ease-out; the exit is shorter than the entrance, so new results never wait on old ones.

Settings: --duration 300 (150 to 1200, step 10; Duration (ms)); --startScale 0.94 (0.5 to 1, step 0.01; Start scale); --stagger 60 (0 to 200, step 5; Stagger (ms)).
Renderer: DOM (CSS and the Web Animations API). Size: 10.1 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/fade-scale.html

### Stagger grid

Stagger grid is a DOM effect: delay grows with distance from the tap. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add stagger-grid.

Tap a paint-chart swatch and every swatch turns a shade of it, in a spreading wave.

Each swatch’s delay is its distance from the tap times a small per-cell step (20 to 40 ms), so one rule turns dozens of changes into one ripple.

Settings: --delayPerCell 28 (5 to 80, step 1; Delay per cell (ms)); --cols 10 (4 to 14, step 1; Columns).
Renderer: DOM (CSS and the Web Animations API). Size: 8.1 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/stagger-grid.html

### Easing curves race

Easing curves race is a DOM effect: same distance, same time, four easing curves. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add easing-race.

Four billing toggles switch together over the same distance and time; only the easing curve differs.

Linear, ease-in, a strong ease-out and a spring run side by side; in the first tenth of a second ease-out is nearly there, which is why it feels responsive.

Settings: --duration 1000 (400 to 3000, step 50; Duration (ms)); --stiffness 180 (40 to 400, step 5; Spring stiffness); --damping 14 (4 to 40, step 1; Spring damping).
Renderer: DOM (CSS and the Web Animations API). Size: 5.5 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/easing-race.html

### 3D card flip

3D card flip is a DOM effect: rotateY on a spring, with the back face hidden. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add card-flip.

At checkout the card preview turns over when the CVC field gets focus, and back afterwards.

Two faces sit back to back with backface-visibility hidden and perspective on the parent; a spring drives the angle, so it overshoots slightly and settles.

Settings: --perspective 900 (300 to 2000, step 10; Perspective (px)); --stiffness 160 (40 to 400, step 5; Stiffness); --damping 13 (4 to 40, step 1; Damping).
Renderer: DOM (CSS and the Web Animations API). Size: 8.8 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/card-flip.html

### Anticipation & follow-through

Anticipation & follow-through is a DOM effect: crouch before the hop, wobble after the landing. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add anticipation.

A product hops into the bag icon, crouching first and stretching in flight, while the handle swings on.

The crouch is anticipation and the handle’s swing after the bag stops is follow-through, both damped curves computed per frame; without them the hop feels pushed, not jumped.

Settings: --anticipation 0.25 (0 to 0.6, step 0.01; Crouch depth); --overshoot 0.18 (0 to 0.5, step 0.01; Landing overshoot).
Renderer: DOM (CSS and the Web Animations API). Size: 9.1 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/anticipation.html

### List reorder (FLIP)

List reorder (FLIP) is a DOM effect: FLIP reorder; rising rows pass above falling ones. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add list-reorder.

A running club’s leaderboard re-ranks by distance, pace or climb, and each runner glides to their new place.

FLIP: measure each row, reorder, transform each back to its old spot and animate to zero; rows moving up pass above those going down.

Settings: --duration 300 (150 to 1200, step 10; Duration (ms)); --lift 0.03 (0 to 0.08, step 0.005; Lift).
Renderer: DOM (CSS and the Web Animations API). Size: 8.5 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/list-reorder.html

### Add & remove

Add & remove is a DOM effect: the gap closes after the item leaves, and opens before it returns. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add add-remove.

A removed bag item fades out, then the rows below close the gap; Undo reverses both steps.

Rows never animate height: they’re measured before and after and slid with a staggered transform (FLIP), and leaving then collapsing means nothing jumps.

Settings: --duration 300 (150 to 800, step 10; Slide (ms)); --stagger 30 (0 to 120, step 5; Stagger (ms)).
Renderer: DOM (CSS and the Web Animations API). Size: 9.5 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/add-remove.html

### Number ticker

Number ticker is a DOM effect: each digit is a 0–9 strip that rolls to its value. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add number-ticker.

A revenue card switches range and each digit rolls to its new value like an odometer.

A button’s dark fill sweeps in from the side the cursor entered and out the side it leaves.

A filled copy of the button is revealed with a clip-path inset from the entry edge, then collapses onto the exit edge from wherever the last sweep got to.

Settings: --duration 240 (80 to 600, step 10; Enter (ms)); --exit 200 (80 to 600, step 10; Exit (ms)).
Renderer: DOM (CSS and the Web Animations API). Size: 8.3 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/directional-fill.html

### Sliding underline

Sliding underline is a DOM effect: one underline travels between links and stretches. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add underline-slide.

One nav underline slides to the hovered link and returns to the current page when the cursor leaves.

Its two ends ride separate springs, the leading end quicker, so it stretches toward the target; drawn with translateX and scaleX only.

Settings: --stiffness 260 (60 to 800, step 10; Stiffness); --stretch 0.45 (0 to 0.85, step 0.05; Stretch).
Renderer: DOM (CSS and the Web Animations API). Size: 8.0 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/underline-slide.html

### Lit border

Lit border is a DOM effect: card edges catch a light that follows the cursor. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add lit-border.

Cards in a dark grid light up around the cursor, with neighbours catching spill on their nearest edges.

Each card places a radial gradient in its own coordinates; a mask limits one copy to a 1px border while another tints the surface.

Settings: --radius 220 (80 to 400, step 10; Radius (px)); --glow 0.2 (0 to 0.4, step 0.01; Surface glow).
Renderer: DOM (CSS and the Web Animations API). Size: 7.4 KB. Reduced motion: no. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/lit-border.html

### Dock magnify

Dock magnify is a DOM effect: icons swell around the cursor and push apart. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add dock-magnify.

Dock icons swell as the cursor passes, largest under it and tapering over a few neighbours.

Scale follows a cosine falloff with distance, and each icon’s offset is computed from the new sizes so the row spreads exactly as wide as it grew; transforms only.

Settings: --magnify 1.8 (1 to 2.6, step 0.05; Magnify); --range 140 (60 to 260, step 5; Range (px)).
Renderer: DOM (CSS and the Web Animations API). Size: 10.0 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/dock-magnify.html


## Micro & loading

### Toggle spring

Toggle spring is a DOM effect: the knob stretches while it travels. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add toggle.

Notification switches flip one at a time, each knob stretching along its travel and snapping round on landing.

The knob rides a spring, with a scaleX anchored at its trailing edge that grows with speed; the track colour follows knob position, not a timer.

Settings: --stiffness 300 (80 to 800, step 10; Stiffness); --damping 20 (8 to 50, step 1; Damping).
Renderer: DOM (CSS and the Web Animations API). Size: 4.9 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/toggle.html

Like burst is a DOM effect: squash, pop, ring and sparks on one beat. One plain JavaScript file with no dependencies; add it with npx motion-library add like-burst.

A saved product’s heart squashes, pops past full size and settles as a ring and dots fire.

Every part starts on the same frame so it reads as one event, and the sparks pick fresh random angles each time.

Settings: --particles 10 (4 to 24, step 1; Sparks); --spread 1 (0.4 to 2, step 0.05; Spread).
Renderer: DOM (CSS and the Web Animations API). Size: 7.5 KB. Reduced motion: yes. Page: https://ajeckblad.github.io/motion-library/fx/like-burst.html

### Submit to success
